title: Oyastu Forest
intro: This lesson fades out words as the audio plays. Click a sentence to jump back to that point.
sentences: Oyatsu Forest is a historic woodland located behind Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine in Kamakura.
In 1964, during Japan’s rapid economic growth, there was a plan to develop this area into a housing site.
Many local residents, writers, and other supporters opposed the project because they wanted to protect Kamakura’s natural beauty and cultural heritage.
They collected donations and successfully purchased part of the forest, saving it from destruction.
This movement later became known as the “Oyatsu Movement” and led to the establishment of Japan’s first National Trust organization.
It also influenced the creation of the Ancient Capitals Preservation Law in 1966, which helped protect many historic areas in Kamakura.
Today, Oyatsu Forest remains an important symbol of environmental conservation.
It indicates how ordinary citizens can work together to preserve nature and history for future generations.
